title: Made a real-time hex strategy game with Claude, looking for honest feedback on the core loop
author: Zestyclose-Group920
selftext:
Hey all,

I’ve been building Hexhold for a while now. It’s a real-time hex strategy game where one run takes around 30-40 min. The idea and design are mine, and I used Claude for the coding and prototyping. Art and sound are all made in code, no image gen.

The loop is basically:

* build fields on your land (placement matters, neighbours boost or hurt each other)
* send Riders to raid bandit camps, put them on repeat and they keep going while you build
* claim the valley hex by hex, grow from hamlet to town to city
* once you’re a city, the 3 rival lords team up (the Pact) and come for your walls
* win by beating all of them or by raising the Sun Spire and surviving the final siege

There’s a short tutorial for the basics, the rest you’ll figure out as you go :)

Here's a link browser: [https://new-mladost-studio.itch.io/hexhold](https://new-mladost-studio.itch.io/hexhold)

What I’d really like to know:

1. Where did the run drag or feel like waiting?
2. Did the Pact siege feel fair, or did it just kinda happen to you?
3. What would make you start a second run?
4. Bigger one: would this work better as a small multiplayer game, like 4-6 people on one map instead of AI rivals? Or does it feel right as single player?

Brutal is fine, I patch it pretty much daily based on what people say so thanks for trying it out :)
